meta.subtitle: A synthetic worked example showing the shape of a plan: three packs, six events, and one of each evidence grade. No app was walked to produce it, so nothing here is graded OBSERVED. Copy the structure, throw away the content.
meta.the_ask: This is an example, not a real ask. In a real plan this paragraph names how many events you want built and what you are deliberately not asking for.
meta.phase1_intro: 4 events: 3 client, 1 server. Sort by Source to split the mobile ticket from the backend ticket.

governance.title: What this is
rows: The single source of truth for what this product measures. One property, all platforms, identical event names everywhere.
Tab 2 is the build ask. Tab 4 defines the attribute packs. Tab 5 is the full target state. Anything not graded OBSERVED is a design to confirm, not a spec to implement.

phase1_config: Set the user id at sign-in and clear it at sign-out. Without stable identity there is no retention measurement at all.
Custom definitions are almost never backfilled, so anything registered after launch is blank for every day before it.

packs.name: Core context (auto-collected)
packs.purpose: What the SDK attaches to every event. Documented so nobody re-sends it.

params.name: platform / os_version / app_version
params.notes: Collected automatically; re-sending it is a naming-rule violation.

packs.name: Content
packs.purpose: The title in context. Attached by every playback and browse event.

params.name: content_id
params.notes: The join key for every content-level analysis.

params.name: content_type
params.notes: The catalogue split behind every funnel.

params.name: genre
params.notes: Display context; absence should never fail QA.

params.name: duration_sec
params.notes: Playable content only; undefined for a browse card.

packs.name: Playback
packs.purpose: How a session of watching actually went. Attached by the playback events only.

params.name: position_sec
params.notes: Where in the title the event happened.

params.name: quality
params.notes: Delivered quality at the moment of the event.

params.name: is_autoplay
params.notes: Only when playback started without an explicit press.

user_properties.name: plan_tier
user_properties.update: on sign-in and on any plan change
user_properties.why: Every metric splits by tier, and tier drives the whole monetisation read.

user_properties.name: is_internal
user_properties.why: Staff traffic otherwise looks like a tracking bug in month one.

events.name: content_viewed
events.trigger: A title detail page finishes rendering
events.screens: no screen - this example is synthetic, nothing was walked
events.why_p1: The denominator of the browse-to-play funnel. Without it, play counts have nothing to divide by.
events.work: FE - one line on the detail screen
events.notes: entry_point is what tells you whether recommendations are earning their place. Graded INFERRED because this example was written from a description, not from a walkthrough.

events.name: playback_started
events.trigger: The first frame renders, not when the play control is pressed
events.screens: no screen - this example is synthetic, nothing was walked
events.why_p1: The core value moment. Firing it on first frame rather than on press is deliberate: the gap between the two is where startup failures hide.
events.notes: Do not fire on press. A press that never becomes a frame is a failure, not a play. Graded INFERRED because this example was written from a description, not from a walkthrough.

events.name: playback_failed
events.trigger: Playback aborts before or during the stream
extra_params: error_reason: drm | network | geo_blocked | decode | unknown
events.screens: no screen - this example is synthetic, nothing was walked
events.why_p1: Failed plays are invisible today and look identical to users who changed their mind.
events.notes: PARTIAL: the surface was seen but only the network branch was reproduced. The other error_reason values come from the player SDK docs and need confirming against the real error codes.

events.name: subscription_renewed
events.trigger: The billing system confirms a successful renewal
events.screens: no screen - server-side, needs a real billing cycle to observe
events.why_p1: Renewal is the actual retention outcome; app engagement is only a leading indicator of it.
events.work: BE - one hook on the billing webhook
events.notes: UNVERIFIABLE: nobody subscribed during discovery, so the billing states are designed from the provider docs. Confirm the real webhook payload before building.

key_events.name: playback_started
key_events.why: The core value moment of a streaming product.

key_events.name: subscription_renewed
key_events.why: The retention outcome that revenue actually depends on.

open_questions: This example plan was written from a description; no app was walked, so every event is INFERRED or UNVERIFIABLE.
In a real engagement the first ask is a build or a staging environment to walk. Without one, the plan is a proposal.
error_reason values come from the SDK docs, not from observed failures. Only the network branch was reproduced.
Ask engineering for the real error-code list from the player integration and replace the enum wholesale.
The renewal event and its states are designed from provider documentation; no subscription was ever active during discovery.
Ask for a sample webhook payload and the full set of billing states.
roadmap: The value moment, its denominator, its failure mode, and the revenue outcome.
Now. One client release plus one backend hook.
A browse-to-play funnel, a reliability number that does not exist today, and renewal tied to behaviour.
Playback depth and completion, list management, search, recommendation slates.
When Phase 1 raises a question you cannot answer.
Depth behind the Phase 1 headline numbers.
cuts: A progress ping every 30 seconds is the highest-volume event in any streaming plan and it is billable on most platforms. Completion can be derived from a single completion event, so heartbeats wait until someone needs second-by-second retention curves.
